title: The Daily Five
dek: Five questions from this week's verified Israel Sports Pulse stories, spanning judo, artistic swimming and Israeli footballers at home and abroad.

questions.question: In Rio de Janeiro on 29 August 2013, how did Yarden Gerbi seal Israel's first-ever World Judo Championships gold medal?
answers: A 43-second ippon victory over reigning European champion Clarisse Agbegnenou in the final
A points decision in a full five-minute final
A golden-score victory after extra time
A walkover after her opponent withdrew injured
questions.explanation: Gerbi won all five of her bouts that day by ippon, capping the run with a 43-second final win over France's Clarisse Agbegnenou at the Ginásio do Maracanãzinho.

questions.question: Where did Israel's Lior Makmel and Yogev Dagan finish in the mixed duet technical final at the 2026 European Aquatics Championships in Paris?
questions.explanation: The Israeli pair scored 193.8017 points to finish fifth, behind gold medallists Isabelle Thorpe and Ranjuo Tomblin of Great Britain.

questions.question: What happened after Dor Turgeman scored New England Revolution's second goal against CF Montréal on 1 August 2026?
answers: He celebrated with a defiant gesture toward Montreal fans who had directed antisemitic abuse at him
He was immediately substituted for his own safety
He refused to celebrate and apologized to the crowd
questions.explanation: A section of Montreal supporters chanted "Death to Israel" and abused Turgeman, and he responded to his 36th-minute goal with a defiant gesture toward them.

questions.question: Which Israeli club did Kings Kangwa leave to join Panathinaikos in a transfer worth up to €4.5m in late July 2026?
questions.explanation: Kangwa, the reigning Israeli Footballer of the Year, moved from Hapoel Beer Sheva to Panathinaikos on a contract to June 2030.

questions.question: How many consecutive Israeli league titles did Dolev Haziza win during his seven years at Maccabi Haifa before moving to Maccabi Netanya?
questions.explanation: Haziza spent 2019-2026 at Maccabi Haifa, winning three consecutive league titles and once captaining the side, before signing a two-year deal with Maccabi Netanya.
